text:
Alex: Quick heads-up — ran an autowarm smokecheck during last night's autoscale event, and we hit a weird regression when the kernel fallback kicked in. posting quick numbers and logs. :eyes:
Maria: can you paste the hit-rate snapshots?
Alex: sure, short gist:
```
experiment: autowarm-smoke-2026-03-18
seed_traffic: 250rps staged-fanout
initial_kv_hitrate: 0.74
on_kernel_fallback: 0.33
p50_latency_ms: 38 -> 82
observed_batch_size_mean: 12 -> 48
```
Kevin: woah, hit-rate halved once fallback engaged. looks like fallback path is missing prefix normalization / cache keying alignment.
Sara: could also be batching heuristics — bigger batches reduce locality for prefix keys and evict more KV entries in-flight. did you see cache eviction spikes?
Alex: yes eviction spike correlated with batch size jump. eviction_rate went +5x during fallback window.
infra-bot: Run 3481234567-autowarm-smokecheck completed. Logs: https://ci.internal/runs/3481234567 (artifacts archived) :package:
Maria: ok two immediate hypotheses: 1) fallback kernel uses different LRU buckets (bad), 2) fallback path disables prefix normalizer so session-specific tokens leak into keys.
Kevin: i profiled the fallback hotpath briefly — kernel chooses a different kv-serialize format to avoid lock contention, which changed how we encode prefix length. that would explain mismatch.
Sara: interim mitigation idea: make warmers emit canonicalized keys (strip user-session ids) so both fastpath & fallback hit same cache entries. low-risk and deployable as a runtime flag.
Ryan: agreed. also want to try reducing batch window during warmers to keep batch_size <= 8. should preserve locality.
Alex: plan proposal:
- add runtime flag `warmers.canonicalize_keys=true` (default off)
- run a canary autowarm with staged fanout + batch_window=30ms on 1% traffic
- telemetry: prefix_hit_rate, eviction_rate, p50/p95 latency, kernel_selected
Kevin: i'll instrument additional trace spans to capture kernel_selected and kv_key_hash in traces. will add a compact histogram for key cardinality per pod.
Maria: long-term we should ensure kernel selection preserves key encoding compatibility; maybe unify serializer into shared lib.
Sara: agree. but short term let's try the canonicalize_keys flag + smaller batch window. low blast radius.
Alex: who wants the canary run? Kevin + Ryan?
Kevin: i'll own the instrumentation and canary orchestration. Ryan: i'll prep the job and smoke traffic generator (will use synthetic traffic that mirrors top-100 prefixes).
infra-bot: scheduled job `autowarm-canary-1pct` created for 2026-03-19T02:00Z (run id 3481234600).
Maria: add one more check: compare kernel fallback ratio pre/post and ensure fallback doesn't become the default under canary.
Sara: also add a regression alert if prefix_hit_rate drops >10% or eviction_rate increases >2x.
Alex: sweet. Kevin, Ryan, Maria — please post results in this thread when done. I'll follow up with a postmortem if we need a rollout rollback. :thumbsup:
Kevin: ack, will post traces and a tiny dashboard snapshot.
Ryan: prepping generator now, ETA ~3 hours.
Maria: thanks — tagging infra oncall for visibility @sre-oncall
Alex: thanks team. keeping this thread for follow-ups only.
